obligations.title: Original positive population
obligations.selected_claim: Positive powerful integers and original starting-integer count. Powerful includes 1 and excludes 0; squares, proper powers, possible 4-full endpoints and all Pell returns remain in the population.

obligations.title: Canonical source
obligations.selected_claim: Positive b,d,u,v, squarefree b,d and the original consecutive equation. No same-endpoint gcd(b,u)=1 or gcd(d,v)=1 condition; canonical source existence and uniqueness are both available.

obligations.title: Rational coordinates
obligations.selected_claim: Original rational coordinates are (b/d,v/u), with positive denominators from PairSource. Coordinate injection and start injection are separately available.

obligations.title: Shell, scales and source inventory
obligations.selected_claim: Actual boxes use inclusive X<=n<=2X, B<=b<=2B, E<=d<=2E; actualDirectInterval is closed at both ends. This broader shell domain safely covers the manuscript's strict lower endpoint. There is no b<=d or bounded-skew restriction.

obligations.title: Profile and exponent conventions
obligations.selected_claim: Theta=333/1400; all five weights and both chart regimes are retained. Rounded M is an integer ceiling and T is a real quotient; T is not identified exactly with an unrounded power.

obligations.title: One chart-specific integer minor
obligations.selected_claim: The original direct/inverse integer rows, fixed eight-column order and denominator clearing are shared by real and modular branches. Chart selection does not equate the two different chart determinants.

obligations.title: Graph, homogeneous forms and levels
obligations.selected_claim: Actual common degree is max(deg A,deg B); fullGraphResultant is signed integer and its absolute value gives a positive size when nonzero. Primitive signed parameters, evaluated natural gcd, nonzero signed levels, constants and axis cases are explicit.

obligations.title: Reuss source input
obligations.selected_claim: The final specialized k=3,l=2 route proves its needed producer internally and does not assume a Reuss proposition. The listed consumers replace the mathematical role; they are not applications of an implemented general Reuss theorem.

obligations.title: Stewart source input
obligations.selected_claim: Explicit Prop premise for content-one full-affine-degree homogenizations with separable rational affine section, degrees 3..11, signed nonzero level and primitive signed parameter pairs including axes; bound 2800*d^(1+omega(|h|)). Irreducibility is not an input; separable reducible cubics are admitted.

obligations.title: Projective intersection bounds
obligations.selected_claim: No general projective Bezout theorem is claimed. Resultant/nonzero-fibre singular counting and primitive-direction low-factor counting provide sufficient substitutes; the selected conservative route bypasses proper-intersection geometry.

obligations.title: Fixed-degree factor and coefficient heights
obligations.selected_claim: Proved integral factor bounds support both the degree-three graph extraction and bounded-degree coarse factors. Heights are derived for actual divisors; no unbounded coefficient-dependent constant is introduced.

obligations.title: Controlled finite prime lists
obligations.selected_claim: Bertrand-based fixed-length distinct prime lists have fixed comparison constants; prime values vary with the current scale. The family precedes individual sources.

obligations.title: Finite-field polynomial zero bound
obligations.selected_claim: The actual smooth-residue cardinal bound handles both nonzero and zero reduction. If reduction is identically zero, every reduced partial is zero and the smooth set is empty; no blanket nonzero-reduction premise is needed by smooth_label_budget.

obligations.title: Integral one-parameter lifting
obligations.selected_claim: Finite polynomial implicit parametrization over ZMod(p^28), from either nonzero reduced partial, is enough for the same-minor determinant application.

obligations.title: Finite determinant expansion
obligations.selected_claim: Polynomial evaluation determinant vanishes when a^28=0 and all eight nodes are multiples of a; degree<8 remainder and Vandermonde factorization replace an infinite-series Cauchy-Binet argument. Zero divisors and repeated nodes are included.

obligations.title: Real divided-difference estimate
obligations.selected_claim: Exact root-coordinate polynomial divided-difference argument yields all five mixed-row bounds with one uniform constant; terms with at least five error rows vanish. No independent general differentiability theorem is inferred.

obligations.title: Integer row-space/null-vector facts
obligations.selected_claim: Integral whole-row-space relation includes empty populations, fewer than the column count, repetitions, all lower ranks and generic H=1. CF12 height remains preserved.

obligations.title: Homogeneous resultant identities
obligations.selected_claim: Full homogeneous resultant at actual common degree, integral homogeneous adjugate identities and evaluated gcd divisibility include axes. Nonzero follows from rational coprimality and positive actual degree.

obligations.title: Axis-sensitive polynomial root support
obligations.selected_claim: Locally proved use of Mathlib polynomial abc after axis screening excludes the required low-degree pure powers. No external abc hypothesis is added.

obligations.title: Uniform divisor growth
obligations.selected_claim: Uniform divisor subpower estimates apply to the actual nonzero resultant with |R|<=720*X^90. Constants precede varying graphs within the fixed envelope.

obligations.title: Elementary analytic assembly
obligations.selected_claim: Ceil/floor comparisons, finite head, fixed constants and all three logarithmic losses are paid explicitly. Natural aggregation uses a uniform shell envelope and an extra logarithmic loss rather than a general geometric-series theorem.

obligations.title: Normal-form equivalence
obligations.selected_claim: Both directions of positive powerful squarefree-cube/square normal form, with uniqueness, are retained.

obligations.title: Cross-endpoint coprimality
obligations.selected_claim: Cross-endpoint coprimality is derived from the consecutive equation; no forbidden same-endpoint coprimality premise is imposed.

obligations.title: Starts and canonical sources
obligations.selected_claim: Two-sided canonical-source correspondence and uniqueness preserve every original positive start and its cutoff; the final theorem consumes the exact PairCount identity.

obligations.title: Source-to-ratio injection
obligations.selected_claim: Equal reduced rational coordinate pairs imply equality of n,b,d,u,v; start-only injection is separately available and used for cardinal transfers.

obligations.title: Fixed-kernel counting fibre
obligations.selected_claim: Uniform fixed-product Pell theorem counts all original starts with b*d=D, not only one fixed allocation (b,d). This stronger bound supplies both the aggregate complement and fixed-kernel ruling fibre; no Pell-classification premise remains.

obligations.title: Small kernel product
obligations.selected_claim: Finite bound Y*(log2(2N+1)+1) is stronger than the mapped logarithm-squared route. The unconditional real consumer is uniform for X>=32 and every real Y>=0, including fractional/subunit cutoffs; no Y upper bound is needed.

obligations.title: Fixed-multiplier counting fibre
obligations.selected_claim: Actual coprime fixed multiplier ratios give full-degree primitive separable cubic level-one forms; exact Stewart counts them uniformly, including reducible cubics.

obligations.title: Small multiplier product
obligations.selected_claim: Dyadic product labels and the fixed-multiplier fibre theorem count original starts with positive u*v<=Y. The real subpower consumer retains its stated 0<=Y<=4X domain; BoxCounts proves that domain for Y=X^theta.

obligations.title: Paid sets versus residual set
obligations.selected_claim: Local proof fragment in actual_box_source_count: Sk filters b*d<=Y, Su filters u*v<=Y, Sr filters both products>Y, and S is covered by (Sk union Su) union Sr. Overlap is allowed; the set-theoretic cover itself needs no Stewart premise.

obligations.title: Actual-to-nominal size comparison
obligations.selected_claim: Actual box products and nominal scales are related with proved fixed factors. B,E and nominal U,V are >=1/2; four-times nominal upper heights are >=2 and cover all coordinates. Literal prescribed U,V coupling belongs to nominal scales.

obligations.title: Residual profile domain
obligations.selected_claim: Both actual small-product cutoffs imply one uniform compact profile BE=X^psi, theta/2<=psi<=(2/3)*(1-theta/2), with fixed endpoint factors paid. Rounded log comparability/slack follows at a profile-uniform threshold; an empty population needs no anchor.

obligations.title: Dyadic box cover
obligations.selected_claim: Local proof fragment in original_shell_source_count: every source has b,d<=floor(3X); labels (log2 b,log2 d) lie in a common finite product range with at most (log2 floor(3X)+1)^2 entries, and every fibre has an actual closed dyadic box. Both kernel orientations and all returns are covered.

obligations.title: Real-profile envelope
obligations.selected_claim: Universal real-profile envelope on [0,2/3], all five branches, exact centre values and m0<=3/16; no finite sample or count premise is used.

obligations.title: Positive prime exponent and strict slack
obligations.selected_claim: Positive uniform prime-scale exponent and strict 25*delta margin are established with explicit delta/profile domains before rounding.

obligations.title: Ceiling and scale comparison
obligations.selected_claim: Integer ceiling bounds, profile-uniform positive T lower bound and all mixed-term bounds are proved. BoxCounts establishes the exact M*T=X^(theta+delta) identity with M>0; T is not exactly the unrounded x^q.

obligations.title: Source-faithful Reuss application
obligations.selected_claim: Specialized internal k=3,l=2 producer supplies a nonzero integral F of uniform degree/height on each actual finite interval population; one common family of <=3M+1 closed original intervals is then summed. Degree/height constants precede X, profile, box, interval and population. Kernel-one/multiplier-one cases are included without invoking Reuss.

obligations.title: Factor instances and heights
obligations.selected_claim: For each original interval, uniform_primitive_factor_cover constructs <=D actual primitive integral rationally irreducible divisors with uniform coefficient heights and rational-zero coverage. IntervalCounts sums these factors and BoxCounts sums the original interval family. The nested sums charge repeated polynomials separately across intervals, without a polynomial census.

obligations.title: Singular-source count
obligations.selected_claim: Rationally irreducible factors, including geometrically reducible cases, have <=2D^3 singular rational points and corresponding original starts. Actual-degree resultant/nonzero-fibre argument and source injection replace general projective Bezout.

obligations.title: Bounded chart localisation
obligations.selected_claim: Both direct and inverse root nodes are derived from one actual original closed direct interval with M<=X. Unit coordinates and endpoints remain; no independent second M-sized interval cover or chart inventory appears.

obligations.title: Uniform nonzero witness
obligations.selected_claim: A selected cleared partial yields a nonzero integer witness at every actual nonsingular source, with polynomial height uniform from fixed D,H,C. The source cutoff n<=2X is handled by the shell adapter, rather than assuming rounded-scale monotonicity.

obligations.title: Fixed-length candidate prime list
obligations.selected_claim: Fixed list length and comparison constants are chosen from witness growth and a uniform positive T exponent. At each scale/profile one prime list precedes every allowed polynomial/source; prime values themselves vary with scale.

obligations.title: Every source gets a good prime
obligations.selected_claim: Every nonsingular source has a first good member of the common bounded list, with p not dividing d*u and a nonzero reduced partial. No universally good prime or sourcewise uncharged prime family is assumed.

obligations.title: O(T) smooth labels per factor
obligations.selected_claim: The sum of actual smooth-residue cardinalities over the common prime list is O(T). IntervalCounts constructs original-start fibres using first-good-prime and residue labels and consumes that exact budget.

obligations.title: Integer/rational row identity
obligations.selected_claim: Original direct row is d^3*u times the specified monomial row and inverse row d*u^3 times its specified ordering. Modular denominator factors are units; rational relation evaluation uses the same original coordinates.

obligations.title: Integral smooth parametrisation
obligations.selected_claim: One finite implicit polynomial over ZMod(p^28), from either good partial, represents all actual source lifts in the common smooth residue fibre. The actual-source theorem discharges polynomial vanishing and denominator conditions from explicit source hypotheses.

obligations.title: Generic eight-series divisibility
obligations.selected_claim: Eight polynomial columns evaluated at nodes divisible by a have zero determinant when a^28=0. This finite precision statement supplies the required 0+...+7=28 exponent, including repeated nodes and zero divisors.

obligations.title: p^28 divides the source minor
obligations.selected_claim: For every eight-source selection satisfying actual F-vanishing, good-prime and common-residue hypotheses, p^28 divides both original chart-specific integer determinants. No supplied series or real-normalized determinant premise remains.

obligations.title: All five real mixed terms
obligations.selected_claim: Root-coordinate polynomial determinant bounds give all five mixed error terms at the exact weights (28,21,16,13,12); terms with five or more error rows vanish. Uniform constants cover both charts and mixed row orders.

obligations.title: Restore both integer scales
obligations.selected_claim: Positive actual row/column normalization restores the original integer determinants with direct X^4*(BE)^6 and inverse X^12/(BE)^14 scales. No bounded-skew hypothesis is imposed.

obligations.title: Real bound for the selected minor
obligations.selected_claim: Selected chart at the profile breakpoint bounds the same original eight-row integer minor by the sum of five rounded mixed terms, with one fixed uniform constant. The chart choice does not identify direct and inverse determinants.

obligations.title: Uniform strict integer squeeze
obligations.selected_claim: Fixed coefficients and the strict 25*delta exponent margin yield one profile-uniform threshold before boxes, class labels, primes and row tuples, making the actual bound strictly below p^28. Divisibility is supplied separately.

obligations.title: All eight-row minors vanish
obligations.selected_claim: Actual common source tuple, chart, column order and original denominator clearing bind the real bound and p^28 divisibility for every eight-row selection. No supplied analytic-size premise remains.

obligations.title: One relation for the whole class
obligations.selected_claim: One nonzero integral polynomial precedes all class members. Arbitrary index types, empty/fewer-than-eight classes, repetitions and every lower rank are included. Original rational-coordinate evaluation is proved from positive integer row denominators.

obligations.title: Polynomial height of second relation
obligations.selected_claim: boundedSourceRelation includes coefficient height X^14. This remains a genuine current dependency: class G -> graph coefficients <=X^15 -> nonzero full resultant with |R|<=720*X^90 -> uniform divisor growth.

obligations.title: Generic proper-intersection lemma
obligations.selected_claim: No current paper-target application of the generic 4*deg(F) projective proper-intersection bound is matched. Every smooth class is instead counted through bounded graph/ruling arithmetic.

obligations.title: Generic inherited bidegree
obligations.selected_claim: Generic coordinatewise-degree inheritance for F dividing G is not matched to a current applied target. Current ClassCounts decomposes the bounded class relation G directly.

obligations.title: Low-bidegree graph/ruling normal form
obligations.selected_claim: Actual input is boundedSourceRelation inverse X G: nonzero, support <=(3,1) or <=(1,3), coefficients <=X^14. Degree<=3 sections, primitive gcd removal and proved integral factor height yield boundedGraphData with coefficients <=X^15 and <=3 common-factor rulings. Degenerate zero sections, actual degree zero, both orientations and positive source coordinates are retained.

obligations.title: Uniform arithmetic ruling count
obligations.selected_claim: Fixed-kernel and fixed-multiplier ratio fibres count coordinate rulings; actual degree-zero graph reduces to the partner-coordinate ruling. Counts retain all original starts and use logarithmic subpower absorption, not a small-product aggregate bound at a large fixed product.

obligations.title: Positive resultant and evaluated gcd
obligations.selected_claim: At positive actual common degree max(deg A,deg B), the full signed integer resultant is nonzero; absolute value is positive and the evaluated natural gcd divides it at every primitive signed parameter pair including axes. The resultant is fixed before parameters.

obligations.title: Exact source pullback and signs
obligations.selected_claim: Actual canonical sources yield the direct degree-two-gcd level and both inverse signed degree-three-gcd levels with primitive signed parameters. Reconstruction and source-ratio injection control the transfer to original starts.

obligations.title: Corrected content and reduced level
obligations.selected_claim: The coefficient gcd content c divides the admitted signed level +/-g^ell; the reduced signed h is a nonzero integer and |h| divides g^ell, with g dividing the nonzero resultant and ell in {2,3}. Fixed c is retained before level/sign aggregation.

obligations.title: Pullback factor dispatcher
obligations.selected_claim: Actual primitive pullback factor preparation, axis-sensitive polynomial abc and pure-power exclusion derive the exhaustive fixed factor dispatch: high primitive rationally irreducible factor degree3..11, or two admissible low factors. Factor choice precedes levels.

obligations.title: Admissible factor-level Thue count
obligations.selected_claim: High-factor admissibility derives content-one full-degree homogenization and separability from the selected primitive rationally irreducible factor; nonzero signed levels and primitive signed parameters are explicit before the precise Stewart application.

obligations.title: Low-degree level curves have no common component
obligations.selected_claim: Actual selected low factors satisfy nonproportionality of homogeneous forms, including quadratic versus square of linear. Primitive-direction elimination/counting provides the needed finite level fibres without a general level-curve no-common-component theorem.

obligations.title: Low-degree level-pair count
obligations.selected_claim: Direct homogeneous primitive-direction arguments bound signed primitive fixed-level fibres by 2 or 4, including axes/infinity, then yield 16*tau(|h|)^2. Later graph-parameter/source injection transfers parameter counts to original starts.

obligations.title: Uniform divisor-level budget
obligations.selected_claim: The fixed-c relation c*h=+/-g^ell is used before enumerating gcd/sign labels. All admitted labels, both signs and selected factor levels are charged, yielding 123232*tau(|R|)^8 uniformly. Prime support of h transfers through h|g^ell and g|R; h|R is not assumed.

obligations.title: Graph resultant height
obligations.selected_claim: The actual class pipeline uses boundedSourceRelation coefficients <=X^14, integral graph coefficients <=X^15, actual common degree <=3 and nonzero full resultant |R|<=720*X^90. Generic factor/resultant estimates support these instantiated bounds.

obligations.title: Uniform nonconstant graph count
obligations.selected_claim: Uniform original-source subpower count holds for actual boundedGraphData (degree<=3, coefficient envelope X^15, resultant <=720*X^90). Constants precede all graph choices and sources in that fixed envelope; both signs and source injection are included.

obligations.title: Generic low-bidegree component count
obligations.selected_claim: bounded_graph_ruling_class_subpower is generic over boundedGraphData at the fixed X^15 envelope; rounded_class_source_subpower derives that data from the actual bounded X^14 class relation G. It counts every smooth class, including rulings and constant graphs.

obligations.title: Proper-intersection class application
obligations.selected_claim: The O_D(1) proper-intersection assigned-class application is not used or claimed. The actual interval theorem applies graph/ruling subpower arithmetic to every smooth class.

obligations.title: Common-component application on F
obligations.selected_claim: No matching once-per-coarse-factor F count is asserted from F dividing a class relation G. Current source counts concern bounded G graphs or whole smooth classes.

obligations.title: Once-per-factor accounting split
obligations.selected_claim: No proper/common once-per-factor dichotomy is claimed. Actual interval counts cover every source using singular/nonsingular and first-good-prime/residue fibres, then sum bounded factors and original intervals.

obligations.title: Complete raw box inventory
obligations.selected_claim: Actual interval bound K*T*X^eta includes the fixed singular cost. One common family <=3M+1<=4M yields the conservative M*T*X^eta contribution. With exact M*T=X^(theta+delta), compact_box_source_count concludes K*X^(theta+delta+eta).

obligations.title: Absorb component and singular costs
obligations.selected_claim: Singular constants are absorbed using T>=1 and X^eta>=1. In full BoxCounts choose e=epsilon/3 and delta=min(1,e), include both complements, then bound every contribution by X^(theta+epsilon). This pays the conservative class loss explicitly.

obligations.title: Full shell count
obligations.selected_claim: Both small-product complements, residual compact profiles, produced interval polynomials, all dyadic kernel boxes and their two logarithmic losses are paid. One uniform threshold/constant precedes every closed original shell population, with exponent theta+epsilon.

obligations.title: Positive natural-cutoff theorem
obligations.selected_claim: For each epsilon>0 one C>0 precedes ALL natural N>=1, bounding the canonical original PairCount N by C*N^(333/1400+epsilon). Every positive original start is assigned log2 n; low shells are bounded by one fixed finite head and the additional logarithmic loss is paid.

obligations.title: Real-cutoff manuscript adapter
obligations.selected_claim: For each epsilon>0 one C>0 precedes ALL real X>=1, bounding PairCount(Nat.floor X) by C*X^(333/1400+epsilon). Floor membership is the exact original positive start cutoff; no finite prefix, return, orientation, square or overlap exclusion is introduced.

obligations.title: Original population
obligations.selected_claim: Original positive starts and exact PairCount; no first-birth, square/proper-power, kernel orientation, endpoint overlap or Pell-return restriction. Same-endpoint b-u coprimality is absent.

obligations.title: Actual box to analytic profile
obligations.selected_claim: Actual products imply compact profile and comparable nominal product logs at one uniform threshold. Fixed dyadic factors and log16 budget are paid; scaled upper heights do not inherit literal nominal coupling.

obligations.title: One original cover
obligations.selected_claim: One common <=3M+1 closed original interval family, each actual finite population receives an internal bounded-height polynomial; factors are counted in nested per-interval sums. Both chart localizations come from that same direct interval.

obligations.title: Uniform prime family
obligations.selected_claim: Fixed list length and comparison constants precede sources; primes vary with scale. Actual shell cutoff n<=2X is retained at original roundedScale X, with first-good membership and smooth labels derived.

obligations.title: One integer minor
obligations.selected_claim: Same eight-source tuple, selected chart, original column order and integer row factors bind p^28 divisibility and strict real bound. The modular route is finite precision over ZMod(p^28), not an asserted infinite convergent series.

obligations.title: Whole class
obligations.selected_claim: All eight-row selections vanish, then one nonzero integral relation annihilates all class rows, including empty/small/repeated/lower-rank populations. Coefficient height X^14 remains part of the conclusion.

obligations.title: Geometric branch
obligations.selected_claim: The current route does not split F-divides-G versus proper intersections. It counts every smooth class via graph/ruling arithmetic.

obligations.title: Graph input
obligations.selected_claim: Actual class G has boundedSourceRelation coefficients X^14; degree-three graph extraction gives coefficients X^15 and full resultant |R|<=720*X^90. Actual degree, coprimality, axes, rulings, constants and signs are retained.

obligations.title: Arithmetic budget
obligations.selected_claim: Nonzero signed resultant, g|R, fixed c*h=+/-g^ell, |h| divides g^ell, exhaustive selected factors and primitive signed parameter/source injection give the uniform divisor budget. Precise Stewart is the external premise; raw c|R and h|R are not assumed.

obligations.title: Component inventory
obligations.selected_claim: Every smooth label pays X^eta; bounded factors and one interval family are summed. The actual bound is conservative M*T*X^eta with singulars already absorbed, not once-per-F common-component accounting.

obligations.title: Global uniformity
obligations.selected_claim: Constants and thresholds precede all varying boxes, factors, labels and source populations. Box epsilon allocation, both complements, two kernel-label logarithms, original-start shell logarithm and finite head are paid.

obligations.title: Manuscript endpoint
obligations.selected_claim: One C before all N>=1 or real X>=1; PairCount(floor X) has exact real membership. Precise Stewart alone remains an explicit mathematical premise.

historical_text_annotations.note: The carried source claim mentions a strict lower manuscript endpoint. That describes the earlier manuscript: current section3.3 and LP04 both use inclusive x <= n <= 2x, as does the selected Lean box. No current endpoint discrepancy remains.

The historical Cauchy-Binet label is retained as an identifier. Current section6.2 and LP11 follow the actual monic-remainder/Vandermonde implementation; the row remains a sufficient scope or route variant.
